title: recursive shared block + Mirror depth modulation
hypothesis: A tied nonlinear block with one learned Givens coordinate per depth step recovers step-specific function composition with fewer serialized bytes, beating hard tying and same-byte scalar step gates; compare with static and input-conditioned generated LoRA.
mirror_coordinate: one Givens angle per depth step on hidden and block output
logical_multiplicity: four layer-specific logical operations from one physical block
teacher: four residual recurrent steps using a common block conjugated by independent per-step Givens rotations
controls: tied plus static rank-1 per-step LoRA
tied plus input-conditioned generated rank-1 LoRA

development.selection_metric: mean development MSE across all methods

storage.serialization: torch.save state_dict plus deterministic config JSON

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror MSE <=1.10x untied, <=0.10x hard-tied, <=0.90x scalar gate, and Mirror payload <=0.75x untied. Compare static and generated LoRA; if either is within10% MSE at equal/lower bytes, not Mirror-specific.
failure_gate: Mirror misses the quality gate or static/generated LoRA or same-byte gate matches within10% MSE at equal/lower bytes.
boundaries: teacher deliberately aligned to per-step Givens views
hypernetwork is a small linear coefficient controller, not full Ouroboros reproduction
